userStories.title: Resolve and clamp chat effort levels per model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make chat effort capabilities follow model metadata from catalog discovery through session switching.

**Motivation** — The catalog marks `medium` unsupported for several models (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3`, `hy3`, ...).

**Approach** — `src/chat/chat-effort.ts` — read-only: `EFFORT_LEVELS` (all eight, canonical order), `isEffortLevel`, `modelEffort`, `withEffort`.
- Target: `cycleEffort(level: EffortLevel, step: 1 | -1, levels: readonly EffortLevel[] = EFFORT_LEVELS): EffortLevel` steps within `levels`. When `level` is not in `levels`, step `1` returns the first entry whose `EFFORT_LEVELS` rank is higher than `level`'s (wrapping to `levels[0]`); step `-1` returns the last entry with a lower rank (wrapping to the last entry).
- New `export type SupportedEffort = Exclude<EffortLevel, "default">` (derived from nax-agent's `THINKING_LEVELS`, already imported here). `ThinkingLevel` from `@nathapp/nax-ai` may be named only under `src/agents/catalog/` (`check:nax-ai-imports`), so every chat-side signature below uses `SupportedEffort`; nax-ai's `ThinkingLevel` is structurally the same union.
- New `effortLevelsFor(supported: readonly SupportedEffort[] | undefined): readonly EffortLevel[]`: `["default", ...entries of supported in EFFORT_LEVELS order]`; `EFFORT_LEVELS` when `undefined`; `["default"]` for `[]`.
- New `clampEffort(level, levels)`: `level` when listed (`default` always is); otherwise the listed non-default level nearest in `EFFORT_LEVELS` rank, a tie going to the lower one (mirrors nax-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`); `default` when no non-default level is listed.
- New `clampModelEffort(model: string, levels: readonly EffortLevel[]): string` = `withEffort(model, clampEffort(modelEffort(model), levels))`.
- All exported from `src/chat/index.ts` beside the existing effort exports.
`src/agents/catalog/index.ts` (the only nax-ai importer): new `lookupThinkingLevels(provider: string, model: string): Promise<readonly ThinkingLevel[] | undefined>` (the one site that names nax-ai's `ThinkingLevel`), same fail-open contract as `lookupContextWindow`: `catalog.model(provider, model)?.thinkingLevels`, `undefined` on miss, load failure or throw.
`src/chat/chat-models.ts`: new `chatEffortLevels(input: { config; models: readonly string[]; lookupThinkingLevels }): Promise<ReadonlyMap<string, readonly EffortLevel[]>>` keyed by base model (`provider/id`, no effort suffix); a `config.agent.native.catalogOverrides` entry's `thinkingLevels` wins over the catalog; a model that neither declares is left out.
`src/cli/chat.ts`: `_chatCommandDeps` gains `lookupThinkingLevels`; the command composes the map for the model choices plus the session's starting model (when `--model` names one) and passes it as `ChatHostDeps.effortLevels`. A model outside the map (for example a resumed session's model that is not among the choices) falls back to `EFFORT_LEVELS`; that is intended.
`src/chat/chat-host.ts`: `ChatHostDeps` gains `readonly effortLevels?: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly EffortLevel[]>`. `ChatHost` gains the **optional** method `effortLevels?(model: string): readonly EffortLevel[]` (optional like `agents?` and `history?`, so inline test hosts keep compiling); the native host returns the map entry for the base model, else `EFFORT_LEVELS`. Callers read `host.effortLevels?.(model) ?? EFFORT_LEVELS`. `switchTo({ model })` passes the requested model through `clampModelEffort`.

**Scope** — In: effort algorithms, catalog seam, override precedence, CLI composition, optional host capability and switch clamp. Out: picker/slash/key consumers belong to US-002; Changing nax-ai's `clampThinkingLevel` or the pi-ai catalog data. Changing effort handling in `nax run` / `nax plan` profiles: only the chat TUI changes. Extend chat-effort, chat-models, CLI chat, host switch and existing catalog context-window tests; existing two-argument cycleEffort tables continue passing. Exact createChatHost deps assertions accept the new map while models remains unchanged.

**Interface** — `export type SupportedEffort = Exclude<EffortLevel, "default">`; `cycleEffort(level: EffortLevel, step: 1 | -1, levels: readonly EffortLevel[] = EFFORT_LEVELS): EffortLevel`; `effortLevelsFor(supported: readonly SupportedEffort[] | undefined): readonly EffortLevel[]`; `clampModelEffort(model: string, levels: readonly EffortLevel[]): string`; `lookupThinkingLevels(provider: string, model: string): Promise<readonly ThinkingLevel[] | undefined>`; `chatEffortLevels(input: { config; models: readonly string[]; lookupThinkingLevels }): Promise<ReadonlyMap<string, readonly EffortLevel[]>>`.

userStories.title: Use model effort levels in pickers, slash commands and ctrl+t
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Offer only supported effort in chat controls and add a one-key effort cycle with queued combined switches.

**Motivation** — Switching effort today needs `/effort` plus a picker; the user wants one key.

**Approach** — `src/tui/chat/picker-model.ts`: `PickerModelInput` gains `readonly effortLevels?: readonly EffortLevel[]` (absent = `EFFORT_LEVELS`); the `"effort"` picker lists those entries.
`src/tui/chat/useChatPicker.ts`: `modelOf` passes the current model's levels; `cycle` passes the entry model's levels to `cycleEffort`.
`src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`: `effortCommand` validates against the current model's levels.
ctrl+t (ink: `key.ctrl` and `input === "t"`): next = `cycleEffort(modelEffort(model), 1, levels)`. Idle → `runControl(() => host.switchTo({ model: withEffort(model, next) }))`. During a turn → queued; repeated presses advance from the queued model. `queued` becomes `{ mode?: ChatMode; model?: string }`, and `finishTurn` applies a queued mode and a queued effort as **one** `host.switchTo(...)` call whose argument omits absent keys (a mode-only queue still calls `switchTo({ mode })`).
Callers read `host.effortLevels?.(model) ?? EFFORT_LEVELS`.
Failure messages: `/effort <level>` not offered by the model → `effort "<level>" is not available for <model>; use one of: <levels>`; no switch. `/effort <word>` not a level → `unknown effort "<word>"; use one of: <model's levels>`; no switch.

**Scope** — In: picker rows and left/right cycles, /effort validation, ctrl+t, object queue and one combined finishTurn switch. Out: core lookup/clamp belongs to US-001; ctrl+b/footer belongs to US-011; close-confirm rename belongs to US-013. Keep existing all-eight UI fixtures working when effortLevels is absent. Extend effort-command.test.tsx and picker-effort.test.tsx; create effort-keys.test.tsx with a fixture switchTo that updates current().

**Interface** — `readonly effortLevels?: readonly EffortLevel[]`; `queued` becomes `{ mode?: ChatMode; model?: string }`; `host.effortLevels?.(model) ?? EFFORT_LEVELS`; `cycleEffort(modelEffort(model), 1, levels)`.

userStories.title: Release argv deadlines and tee output through the sandbox launcher
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend command execution with a releasable deadline and a resilient per-chunk output observer.

**Motivation** — A long test suite, build or dev server blocks the conversation for the whole `Bash` call (up to `BASH_TIMEOUT_MS`, 300 s), and a dev server cannot run at all.

**Approach** — `src/internal/argv-exec.ts` — `RunArgvOptions` gains:
- `readonly releaseDeadline?: AbortSignal` — on abort the deadline timer is cleared; already aborted at spawn means no deadline timer is armed; `timedOut` then stays `false`. Its listener is removed on every settle path.
- `readonly onOutput?: (stream: "stdout" | "stderr", chunk: Uint8Array) => void` — called with every chunk `drainToEof` reads, in read order, before capture; a throwing callback is swallowed and the drain continues.
`src/sandbox/types.ts`: `LaunchRequest` gains both fields; `src/sandbox/launcher.ts` forwards both to `runArgv` on the wrapped and the unwrapped path, as it forwards `signal`.

**Scope** — In: additive executor and LaunchRequest options, both launcher paths, timer/listener cleanup and output callback exception isolation. Out: Bash background handles and migration of cancellation ownership belong to US-004/005; no change to ordinary timeout, cancellation, bounded capture or orphan cleanup. Extend argv-exec.test.ts and launcher.test.ts with _argvExecDeps timers; retain existing no-options behavior.

**Interface** — `readonly releaseDeadline?: AbortSignal`; `readonly onOutput?: (stream: "stdout" | "stderr", chunk: Uint8Array) => void`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] runArgv with timeoutMs 1000 and a releaseDeadline signal aborted before the fake clock reaches 1000 ms does not kill the command at 1000 ms.
[unit] runArgv with timeoutMs 1000 and a releaseDeadline aborted before 1000 ms resolves with timedOut: false.
[unit] runArgv with an already-aborted releaseDeadline never calls _argvExecDeps.setTimeout with timeoutMs as the delay.
[unit] runArgv with a releaseDeadline that never aborts removes its abort listener from that signal by the time it resolves.
[unit] runArgv with an onOutput spy, for a command printing a to stdout, calls the spy with "stdout" and the bytes of a.
[unit] runArgv with an onOutput spy, for a command printing b to stderr, calls the spy with "stderr" and the bytes of b.
[unit] runArgv with an onOutput that throws on every call still resolves the full stdout of the command.
[unit] runArgv with neither option kills a hung command at timeoutMs and resolves timedOut: true.
[unit] The sandbox launcher's run with releaseDeadline and onOutput set calls _launcherDeps.runArgv with both fields on the wrapped path.
[unit] The sandbox launcher's run with unwrapped: true and both fields set calls _launcherDeps.runArgv with both fields on the unwrapped path.

routing.reasoning: Two optional executor hooks extend the existing timer and drain implementation and are forwarded through two launcher paths; the scope is bounded, but sandbox/process-cancellation safety requires strict TDD.

suggestedCriteria: Aborting the ordinary signal after releaseDeadline was aborted still kills the process group and resolves aborted: true.
runArgv removes the releaseDeadline abort listener when proc.exited rejects.

userStories.title: Move active foreground Bash calls into the background
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Release a pending Bash tool result while retaining its running command, replay tail and future streamed output.

**Motivation** — A long test suite, build or dev server blocks the conversation for the whole `Bash` call (up to `BASH_TIMEOUT_MS`, 300 s), and a dev server cannot run at all.

**Approach** — Foreground call while the port is present: launch with a tool-owned controller that `ctx.signal` aborts, register `port.foreground({ command, moveToBackground })`, keep the most recent `FOREGROUND_REPLAY_BYTES` of `onOutput` chunks, unregister when the call settles. `moveToBackground()` (1) aborts the call's `releaseDeadline`, (2) detaches `ctx.signal` so a later turn cancel no longer kills the command, (3) adopts with `origin: "moved"`, replays the kept chunks to the sink in order, then forwards later ones, and (4) resolves the pending Bash tool call with `{ content: "moved to the background as <id>", isError: false }`; the `moveToBackground(): void` callback itself returns no tool result. `moveToBackground()` after the call settled does nothing.
The interceptor's `postProcess` is not applied to background output. New logic lives in `bash-background.ts` helpers so `createBashTool.run` stays within its `check:complexity` baseline.
Background commands have no deadline; a command moved with ctrl+b drops its 300 s deadline.
Resource caps, named constants beside the code that uses them: `FOREGROUND_REPLAY_BYTES` (1 MiB, the pre-move output kept for replay; oldest bytes dropped first).

**Scope** — In: foreground registration/unregistration, move signal ownership, deadline release, one adoption, ordered bounded replay and early tool return. Out: explicit background launch contract belongs to US-004; session forwarding to US-006; ctrl+b binding and footer to US-011. Preserve no-port foreground behavior. Extend upstream bash-background.ts and create bash-background-move.test.ts with deferred launch settlement and cancellation spies.

**Interface** — `export interface ForegroundCommand { readonly command: string; moveToBackground(): void; }`; `foreground(call: ForegroundCommand): () => void`; `moveToBackground()` releases the tool result with `{ content: "moved to the background as <id>", isError: false }`, while its public method returns void.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With background: port, a foreground run({ command: "bun test" }) calls port.foreground once with command: "bun test".
[unit] With background: port, when a foreground run({ command: "bun test" }) settles, the function port.foreground returned is called once.

[unit] With background: port whose adopt returns sink id bash-1a2b3c4d, calling the registered call's moveToBackground() while runArgv is pending resolves the tool call with content moved to the background as bash-1a2b3c4d.
[unit] With background: port, a tool call moved by moveToBackground() resolves with isError false.
[unit] With background: port, moveToBackground() aborts the releaseDeadline passed to runArgv.

[unit] With background: port, chunks emitted through onOutput before moveToBackground() are appended to the sink in emission order before any later chunk.
[unit] With background: port, when FOREGROUND_REPLAY_BYTES plus 10 bytes are emitted before the move, the replay appended to the sink is at most FOREGROUND_REPLAY_BYTES long.
[unit] With background: port, when more than FOREGROUND_REPLAY_BYTES are emitted before the move, the replay appended to the sink ends with the last emitted byte.
[unit] With background: port, aborting ctx.signal after moveToBackground() does not abort the signal passed to runArgv.
[unit] With background: port, aborting ctx.signal on a foreground call before any move aborts the signal passed to runArgv.
[unit] With background: port, calling moveToBackground() after the foreground call resolved does not call port.adopt.
[unit] Without a background port, a foreground Bash call still forwards ctx.signal unchanged to runArgv, preserving the existing turn-cancellation path.

[unit] With background: port but no move, a foreground Bash call whose launch resolves exitCode 0, stdout x, stderr empty and timedOut false returns content "exit 0\nx\n", preserving the existing formatExecBody framing.

routing.reasoning: Racing foreground completion, process-group cancellation and sandboxed output handoff is security-sensitive lifecycle work.

When a moved launch rejects, its adopted handle's ended resolves a launchError without an unhandled rejection.

userStories.title: Thread background commands through native sessions and export port types
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect the public session host port to the opt-in Bash capability without changing sessions that omit it.

**Motivation** — The user wants to keep chatting while it runs and be told when it ends (user, 2026-10-29).

**Approach** — `src/session/agent-session-types.ts`: `AgentSessionHostPorts` gains `readonly backgroundCommands?: BackgroundCommandPort`.
`src/session/native-backend-options.ts`: the `hostPorts` strict schema accepts `backgroundCommands` validated with `hasMethods(["adopt", "foreground"])`, message `"must implement adopt and foreground"`.
Threading, mirroring `unsandboxedCommands`: `native-backend.ts` passes `raw.hostPorts?.backgroundCommands` into `buildSessionToolSupport` as `backgroundCommands` → `session-tool-support.ts` → `buildCodingToolSupport` → `coding-tool-extras.ts` → `createBashTool({ background })`. Each hop omits the key when absent, through a spread helper like `unsandboxedToolOptions`, so `coding-tool-support.ts` stays within its complexity baseline.
The five port types are exported from the package entry `@nathapp/nax-agent`; the API snapshot `packages/nax-agent/api/nax-agent.api.txt` is regenerated with `bun run api:update`.

**Scope** — In: host-port type and strict schema, complete production threading, named package exports and API snapshot, session-level advertisement/adoption regressions. Out: tool algorithms belong to US-004/005; chat host wiring belongs to US-010; only Bash gains background support, not RunCommand's argv branch. Extend native-backend-options.test.ts and existing native-backend tests; strict unknown hostPorts rejection remains. New _deps hooks, if needed, are internal exports only.

**Interface** — `readonly backgroundCommands?: BackgroundCommandPort`; `BackgroundCommandPort`, `BackgroundCommandHandle`, `BackgroundCommandSink`, `BackgroundCommandEnd` and `ForegroundCommand` are named type exports from `@nathapp/nax-agent`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enable production chat background tasks across session changes and deliver bounded autonomous completion turns.

**Motivation** — The user wants to keep chatting while it runs and be told when it ends (user, 2026-10-29).

**Approach** — Tasks are created only when the host has `deps.resources` (the same condition as nax jobs and the agents provider); production `nax chat` always passes resources. Nax jobs additionally retain their existing naxEntry requirement.
`src/chat/chat-host.ts`:
- `ChatHost` gains `readonly tasks?: ChatBackgroundTasks`, set when `deps.resources` is present.
- All three session-open sites — `startSession` (~line 284), `resumeSession` (~line 374) and `reopen` (~line 412) — pass `backgroundCommands: this.tasks` when tasks exist.
- `toolProviders` order: resource providers, then `nax-jobs` (when present), then `nax-tasks`, then `nax-agents` (when present).
- `src/chat/chat-mcp.ts`: `"nax-tasks"` joins `RESERVED_SERVER_IDS`, so a user MCP server cannot shadow the built-in provider.
- `teardown()` awaits `tasks.stopAll()` **after** `hygiene.close(handle)` (inside `closeSessionAndResources`, before `resources.teardown()`), so no in-flight `Bash` call can adopt a task afterwards. Once `stopAll()` has begun, `adopt` stops the new handle at once and records the task as `stopped`.
`src/chat/open-chat-session.ts`: the request gains `readonly backgroundCommands?: BackgroundCommandPort`; `nativeBackend(...)` receives `hostPorts: { ...(commandShadow), ...(backgroundCommands) }`, each key only when present.
`src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts`: also subscribes to `host.tasks.onChange` (and works when `host.jobs` is absent). When idle, a queued job notice is delivered first; otherwise `host.tasks.peekNotice()` with the same deliver-then-take protocol. A running turn is never interrupted: notices wait for idle. `useJobs` now returns `{ running: readonly ChatJob[]; noteUserTurn(): void }`; it counts consecutive task-notice turns, and at `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TASK_NOTICE_TURNS` stops delivering task notices until `noteUserTurn()` is called. `ChatApp.tsx`'s `submit` (the user-typed path) calls `noteUserTurn()` before `sendTurn`. Job-notice turns neither count nor reset.
Loop guard: after `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TASK_NOTICE_TURNS` (3) task-notice turns in a row with no user-typed message between them, further task notices stay queued until the user sends a message.
`src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`: `/jobs` appends `formatTasksListing(host.tasks.list())`, one line per task `<id> <state> <command>`; nothing when there are no tasks. When `host.jobs` is undefined but tasks exist, `/jobs` shows only the task lines; with neither, today's `jobs are not available in this session`.
Background tasks belong to the chat host, not one session: `/clear`, `/resume`, ctrl+t, shift+tab and `/model` reopen the session and leave tasks running; notices go to the current session. When a background command ends by itself, the agent takes a turn to react. A running turn is never interrupted: the notice waits for it. Several ended tasks coalesce into one notice.

Keeping a background command's session-scoped sandbox state (its `TMPDIR` and command shadow) alive after `/clear`, `/resume` or a model switch closes that session: a command that depends on its session `TMPDIR` after the switch may fail. **Goal** — Replace binary job-close approval with a safe close policy covering both jobs and background commands.

**Motivation** — The user wants to keep chatting while it runs and be told when it ends (user, 2026-10-29).

**Approach** — New `src/chat/close-confirm.ts` — `createCloseConfirm({ hostJobs?, tasks?, asks, logger }): () => Promise<boolean>`:
- Nothing running (no owned jobs, no running tasks) → `true`, no card. Preserve the specified empty-close regression: chains stop with reason `the chat closed`, without asking.

- `leave`: `chains.stop("the chat closed")`, await `tasks.stopAll()`, → `true`.
- `stay`: stops nothing (chains stay active), → `false`.
